thread:
jen-support: Customer hit an import error after upgrading their app dependencies with Poetry. They ran `poetry add redwood-inference[full]` and then `poetry run python -c \"import redwood\"` and got ModuleNotFoundError. Posting logs and minimal repro.

jen-support: Environment: Python 3.10.12, Poetry 1.5.1, macOS, project uses `virtualenvs.in-project = true`.

jen-support: pip output from inside .venv:
```
(.venv) $ pip show redwood-inference
Name: redwood-inference
Version: 0.3.0
Location: /Users/customer/project/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages
Files:
  redwood_inference/__init__.py
  redwood_inference/client.py
  ...
```
But `import redwood` fails, while `import redwood_inference` works.

sam-engineering: Thanks — this looks like a packaging/namespace mismatch (distribution name vs top-level package). Can you paste `poetry.lock` and `pyproject.toml` minimal bits? Also `python -c "import sys; print(sys.path)"` would help.

jen-support: Pasted minimal pyproject:
```
[tool.poetry]
name = "acme-app"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "..."

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.10"
redwood-inference = {version = "^0.3.0", extras = ["full"]}
```
poetry.lock excerpt shows redwood-inference 0.3.0.

alex-r: Confirming what jen said — the package's top-level module is `redwood_inference` for 0.3.0, but many users expect `import redwood`. Looks like 0.3.1 on our internal branch added a compatibility shim `redwood` package that re-exports the public API. Do we have 0.3.1 published? @deps-bot?

deps-bot: Published redwood-inference 0.3.1 to test PyPI at 2025-11-05T14:12Z. Stable PyPI publish pending review.

sam-engineering: Workarounds for the customer while we publish fix:
- short term: `poetry add redwood-inference@0.3.1` (if we publish to PyPI) or `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/repo@fix/shim#egg=redwood-inference` inside their venv
- or `import redwood_inference as redwood` in their code (not ideal)

lina: Can we also patch our install docs to mention the package name mismatch for <=0.3.0? We should avoid users being blocked. Also consider yanking 0.3.0 from PyPI if it will cause mass breakage.

alex-r: Agreed. I'll open a release ticket to cut 0.3.2 that contains the shim and an explicit `packages=['redwood','redwood_inference']` change in setup.cfg/pyproject to ensure both names resolve. Also let's mark 0.3.0 with a note.

jen-support: Customer tried the explicit pip git install workaround and confirmed it fixed their import error. They opted to pin to the git ref for now until we push stable PyPI. They asked what caused it — explained that some builds produced an sdist where the top-level package folder was named `redwood_inference` and we didn't provide `redwood` alias until later.

sam-engineering: For follow-up, add a snippet to support KB: quick fix and recommended upgrade path, plus the `import redwood_inference as redwood` temporary shim for users who can't upgrade immediately.

jen-support: Marking this resolved on the customer side. Filing an internal postmortem/RC to avoid future packaging regressions. :white_check_mark:
